leads.summary: A partial tee write can make migration retry silently accept a truncated administrator config
leads.consequence: On an affected device whose brcmfmac.conf has Omarchy's block plus other user lines, sudo tee truncates the live file before writing. If the write fails or is interrupted after truncation, omarchy-migrate stops and leaves the marker pending, but the next invocation no longer recognizes an exact owned block and exits 0. It then writes a completion marker and does not restore the lost user options. The first attempt requested reboot-required. This is conditional on a partial write failure, not a claim that ordinary writes fail.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus followup-1 reproduced with real tee and runner (review-run5); low likelihood; not published

leads.summary: Cleanup also removes unrelated blank lines and adds a missing final newline
leads.consequence: The two command substitutions strip all trailing LF bytes from both source and rest. If a user has blank lines preceding a trailing Omarchy block, or a blank-only tail after a block, those blank lines vanish; when no nonblank lines survive the migration removes the whole file. A user line following the block without a final newline gains one. This contradicts 'every other line through untouched' and is missed by tests which only grep preserved text. For normal line-terminated config, the block at the start/middle/end, repeated or adjacent blocks still gets removed; a second run no-ops. CRLF and whitespace-altered blocks are intentionally outside exact matching.
leads.triage: overlaps Opus nit (trailing blank lines/final newline normalized); harmless for modprobe

leads.summary: Coordinate firmware installation with open #10306 before narrowing its shared detection gate
leads.consequence: #10306 installs apple-bcm-firmware inside the same branch that this PR narrows to legacy non-T2 IDs. If conflict resolution places #10306's package action inside this PR's branch, fresh iMac19,x with BCM4364 (4464) receives neither the quirk (correct) nor the firmware package (#10306's promised fix). Its separate migration can later repair an existing install, not fresh setup. The raw merge conflicts and no resolved combined script was executable, so this is an integration condition, not a present defect at the pinned head. Keep firmware installation behind its own broad hardware gate.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #10306 diff; Opus rechecked

leads.summary: Open #9803 ships a differently worded Omarchy block that this cleanup cannot recognize
leads.consequence: If #9803 ships before #13024, it writes a four-line quirk with the updated 'firmware WPA handling fails on affected Apple hardware' comment on T2/BCM4364 Macs other than MacBookPro16,1. #13024's cleanup only matches the previous four-line comment or the old two-line T2 block, so those machines retain feature_disable=0x82000 even after a later #13024 update and its migration marker is recorded. If #9803 merges after #13024, its old broad installer would need rebase to avoid reintroducing the option. No automatically valid combined installer exists yet, so confirm the merge order and update ownership matching against both outputs.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #9803 diff; Opus rechecked

leads.summary: New T2 cases do not pin the installer or 1786391100.sh exclusion, despite test comments
leads.consequence: All sampled T2 Wi-Fi IDs (4464, 43dc, 4488) are absent from the new legacy allowlist, so removing the T2 exclusion independently from the installer and legacy migration leaves the full supplicant suite green. The cleanup suite DOES fail when its T2 part of the hardware gate is deleted, at the 43dc check. To pin the first two gates, supply synthetic T2=1 plus an ID in the legacy allowlist (e.g. 43ba), and assert no config, or qualify the comments to say those gates are redundant for known shipped T2 boards. This is test coverage, not an observed production break on documented T2 models.

leads.summary: A prebuilt initramfs containing brcmfmac may keep the old option after a promised reboot
leads.consequence: If brcmfmac is included and initialized in an affected machine's initramfs, Omarchy's mkinitcpio modconf hook has copied the old /etc/modprobe.d/brcmfmac.conf there before this migration removes it. No image rebuild follows this cleanup, so a reboot alone can load the driver with feature_disable=0x82000 again. The default T2 mkinitcpio MODULES list does not explicitly include brcmfmac, so this is not established for stock machines. Check a real affected image's lsinitcpio module/config contents and boot load timing before treating it as a universal defect. #9835 independently includes a persistent mkinitcpio -P obligation for its Apple Silicon cleanup.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus followup-1: brcmfmac not in stock initramfs, loads after switch_root; dropped

leads.summary: Cleanup fixture never exercises the claimed root-only read path
leads.consequence: The fake sudo simply executes commands as the test user and every test config is created by that user. A refactor replacing 'sudo cat' with 'cat' passes these tests, but on a root-only existing config the actual unprivileged migration cannot read its content and exits nonzero under bash -euo pipefail; the update stops and waits for a retry rather than restoring WPA3. Add a stub that differentiates privileged from unprivileged reads, or a safe root-only sandbox fixture.
leads.triage: speculative test hardening; omitted per requirements

leads.summary: Updated legacy migration comment says no installs receive the quirk, but the legacy installer still writes it
leads.consequence: The sentence 'No install gets the quirk from the installer any more' is false for a fresh pre-T2 Apple Mac carrying 43ba/43bb/43bc/43a3. The migration remains the only repair path for existing legacy installs, but this new wording misdocuments the normal install lifecycle. Qualify it as 'No modern or T2 install' or refer only to existing installs.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier automated review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13024#issuecomment-5807751505) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13024#issuecomment-5826785792), checked at `672e034`.

**Verified:** both earlier findings are resolved.

| Earlier item | Status at `672e034` |
|---|---|
| Cleanup skipped an Omarchy block with lines after it | **Resolved** |
| Not every T2 Mac carries BCM4364 | **Resolved** (still no BCM4355 or BCM4377 hardware check) |
| Optional test improvement: T2 exclusion not pinned by tests | **Partly resolved**, see below |
| Documentation note in `1786391100.sh` | **Partly resolved**, see below |

- **Cleanup:** in 35 isolated cleanup shapes with stubbed `lspci`, `sudo` and `omarchy-state`, `1790165000.sh` removes either exact Omarchy block wherever it sits (start, middle, end, adjacent or repeated blocks, no final newline). It keeps the other lines' content byte for byte and requests `reboot-required` before the edit, only when something changed. CRLF, trailing-space, reworded and administrator-merged variants are left untouched with no reboot request. Symlinks are written through, an unreadable file fails the migration, and a second run only reads the file. The previous cleanup left an Omarchy block behind in 13 of these shapes. The new "user line after the block" test fails against it. Nine upgrade sequences through the real `omarchy-migrate`, plus one on a local merge with current `quattro`, ended as expected.
- **Chip names:** `43dc` (BCM4355) and `4488` (BCM4377) now match `brcm_hw_ids.h` and kernel commits `69005e67ce54` and `bf8bbd903f07` in the comments, tests and description, and both are out of the legacy list in the installer and `1786391100.sh`.
- The earlier mechanism statements (FWSUP bit 13, SAE bit 19, `SAE_OFFLOAD` advertisement, wpa_supplicant dropping SAE key management) still hold. Both suites pass at `672e034` (18 and 12 assertions) and on the merge with `quattro`, and fail against the base code.

One new issue, two small leftovers and a note on related PRs follow.

### The fix depends on Arch's downstream wpa_supplicant patch, not on upstream

The description says hostap commit `41638606` "is gone from current wpa_supplicant", and the author's reply bases this on `wpa_supplicant.c`. That commit changed `wpa_supplicant/events.c`, and it is still upstream:

| Source | `41638606` present? |
|---|---|
| hostap `hostap_2_12` | yes, `events.c:4928-4944` ("wait for driver port authorized indication") |
| hostap `main` | yes, `events.c:5121-5137`; no upstream revert |
| Arch `wpa_supplicant 2:2.12-1` (built 2026-08-10, served by the Omarchy mirrors) | no, removed by `0008-Revert-Mark-authorization-completed-on-driver-indica.patch`, first shipped in this release |

Mainline brcmfmac reports port authorization only for 802.1X fast-transition roams (`cfg80211.c:6488-6490`), never for firmware-offloaded PSK or SAE connects. With `41638606` active, wpa_supplicant waits for an event brcmfmac does not send. This is the failure the t2linux guide still documents.

**Impact:** on current Omarchy the premise holds, because the mirrors serve the patched package. But dropping the quirk on T2 and BCM4364 Macs relies on Arch keeping that downstream revert. A future `wpa_supplicant` release without it would likely break WPA2-PSK and WPA3-SAE association on those Macs again. This is derived from source reading, not a hardware run. The installer comment "Arch's 2.12 carries the fix" is accurate but does not say the fix is downstream.

**Suggested change:** say in the description that upstream hostap 2.12 and main still contain `41638606` and that Arch's `2:2.12-1` reverts it downstream. Name the Arch patch in the installer comment, so a `wpa_supplicant` update that drops it is recognisable as the trigger to revisit this.

### Smaller items

**Optional test improvement:** the reply says deleting the `106b:180[12]` exclusion from any of the three gates "now fails both suites". In mutant runs, deleting it from the installer or from `1786391100.sh` leaves both suites passing. Only the cleanup-gate deletion is caught, by the cleanup suite. With `43dc` and `4488` out of the legacy lists, the legacy-ID check alone keeps the quirk off every tested T2 ID, so the comments at `brcmfmac-supplicant-test.sh:90-92` and `:157-158`, which call the T2 check "the only thing" keeping the quirk off these IDs, are inaccurate. Reword them, or add `T2_HARDWARE=1` cases with a legacy ID such as `43ba` (no quirk written, `1786391100.sh` skips) if the defensive check should be pinned.

**Documentation note:** the new sentence at `1786391100.sh:19-21`, "No install gets the quirk from the installer any more", contradicts the installer, which still writes it on pre-T2 Macs, the only machines this migration now targets. For example: "T2 installs no longer get the quirk from the installer; on pre-T2 Macs the installer covers new installs and this migration covers existing ones."

**Related open PRs:** two open PRs touch the same installer gate.
- [#10306](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/10306) adds `omarchy-pkg-add apple-bcm-firmware` inside the branch this PR narrows to pre-T2 IDs. If it is rebased with the package step left in that branch, a fresh BCM4364 iMac19,x would no longer get the firmware #10306 targets. Gating the firmware install separately from the quirk avoids that.
- [#9803](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/9803), which this PR says it supersedes, writes a differently worded comment above the same `options` line. The cleanup's exact matching would not remove that block if #9803 landed first.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** follow-up source review of `672e034` against the earlier reviewed head `6c7353c`, the merge base and current `quattro`, plus Linux mainline brcmfmac, hostap (2.11, 2.12, main), Arch `wpa_supplicant` packaging and the t2linux wiki. Isolated command-only runs with stubbed `lspci`, `sudo` and `omarchy-state` and redirected config paths covered the cleanup edge cases, installer and migration gate probes, upgrade sequences through the real migration runner, both PR suites and gate-deletion mutants. The stubbed `sudo` runs as the invoking user, so real privilege paths were not exercised. No Apple or Broadcom hardware was available; association behavior is inferred from source, not reproduced. The author's `test/cli` and `omarchy-kernel-migration-test.sh` results were not rerun.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
